newsitem.title: GERMANY: Summary of Ifo Sept German business survey.
newsitem.headline: Summary of Ifo Sept German business survey.

text.p: Following is a summary of key points in the IFO economic research institute's monthly business survey for September (sectors are west German unless otherwise stated, comparisons are against pvs month):
Ifo last week said its business climate index showed a rise to 95.7 in September from 94.4 in August.
Orders levels - stronger, inventory overhang being drawn down
Capacity utilisation - up to 83 percent from 82.2 percent
Business outlook - higher demand boosting output, cutting
Note - Chemicals optimism not yet fed into current business,
metals less optimistic. Pulp and paper more gloomy, but still
set to expand, textiles looking good.
Note - Electricals see good export prospects, vehicles seen
improving over coming months, precision mechanical/optical
sector pessimistic, steel/light metal construction brightening.
Note - Carmakers see improving demand but exports sluggish,
electronics still optimistic, precision mechanical/optical still
Note - Clothing better than in August, but no sign of
recovery, shoes still gloomy but consumer textiles more upbeat.
Business outlook - very sceptical for next half-year
Production plans - production decline to slow
Orders level - down to 2.6 months work, still seen too little
Personnel plans - more job cuts planned
Current business - better, but still unsatisfactory
Prices - only isolated increases can be achieved
Business outlook - no sustained pickup seen
Personnel plans - more cuts planned, workforces seen too high
